Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Sana (Product), Liam (CTO MarineGate), Priya (Data Eng), Jonah (PM), Katherine (SRE), +1 unnamed

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood walked through hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints for MarineGate's search stack. Focus on latency/cost tradeoffs, integration path (API + Console + Optimize recommendations), and security concerns (SSO, audit logs, data retention). Customer to share corpus and query samples for a bench run. Next: quickstart + security pack + 30m benchmarking session.

Topics covered:
- Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint (batching, vector dims, model choice)
- Reranker endpoint (API inputs, label format, top-k reordering)
- Console walkthrough (routes, model pins, rollout)
- Redwood Optimize (batch suggestions, cache and prefix caching)
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pricing & expected cost estimate for 200 qps baseline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for jumping on, i'm avery from redwood inference, i'm the acct exec for this region. quick intros?
[00:12] Liam (MarineGate CTO): liam here, i'll kick off — we run site search for marine datasets and internal docs, want to improve precision on long-tail queries.
[00:20] Priya (MarineGate Data Eng): priya — we're ingesting about 12m docs, embedding store on their managed vec db, about 200 qps peak.
[00:28] Jonah (PM): jonah — main success metric is increase in click-through and reduce time-to-answer, also keeping median latency under 200 ms.
[00:36] Avery: perfect thanks. diego will do technical deep-dive on the API and rerank flow, i'll cover pricing and next steps.
[00:45] Diego (Redwood SE): great, i'll share screen — first slide is high-level flow: query -> embeddings retrieval -> candidate set -> Redwood reranker hosted endpoint -> final results. we support/um both dense retrieval and hybrid scoring. note: the embedding dims we recommend are 768 or 1536 depending on model family, but if you use a 384d that's fine for smaller docs.
[01:12] Katherine (SRE): quick q — what about kv cache behavior for beam searches or multi-turn? do you store kvs between calls?
[01:21] Diego: for hosted reranker API we don't maintain per-customer KV across separate requests. it's stateless per call; caching is at the prefix/KV cache layer for generation endpoints but for rerank we accept full context plus candidates. that said our console can enable prefix caching for chat flows, sorry that's a little mixing of features.
[01:45] Jonah: can you show an API sample for rerank? format?
[01:50] Diego: sure — (screen) payload is basically: query string, candidates array with doc ids and embeddings or raw text, optional labels for training, and a rerank_config block to pin model/version and thresholds. response contains scores and reordered ids. i'll paste the exact curl in notes after — it's in the quickstart.
[02:22] [crosstalk] Priya: and embeddings — do we push vectors or do you do on-the-fly? we currently push vectors to a vector db.
[02:30] Diego: you can do either. hosted embeddings endpoint accepts batch upsert and returns vector ids; many teams prefer storing vectors in their vector db and sending candidates with embeddings to reranker to avoid double lookup. tradeoff is network vs storage.
[02:48] Avery: important for cost: if you push embeddings via our hosted endpoint you pay per-embed unit; if you store elsewhere and send embeddings into reranker you pay for the reranker scoring tokens/compute. we'll run estimates based on your 12m docs and 200 qps.
[03:05] Liam: curious abt model selection — what's default? we want predictable latency.
[03:12] Diego: default for embeddings is redwood-embed-1536-v1 (we called it rwd-embed-1 internally). for rerank we have a light family and heavy family. light models give 2-3x lower latency, slightly lower MRR on some corpora. you can pin a variant in the console per route and set a canary to test quality. note: some of the model names in the docs may show as, uh, rwin-opt or rwd-slim in older decks, ignore that.
[03:42] Jonah: can you demo the console route config?
[03:45] Diego: yes (screen). in console you create a route mapping for /search-forward, select model for embeddings and rerank, choose top_k retrieval size, set batching windows and max tokens, and configure fallback model for capacity issues. you can also enable "automatic batching" from the Optimize tab which suggests batch size based on observed latencies.
[04:15] Priya: does automatic batching add latency for singletons? we have a lot of tail single-user queries.
[04:20] Diego: Optimize simulates request distribution and recommends a batch config with a fixed microbatch delay — you can cap it. for heavy tail you'd set minimal batch window (like 5-10 ms) to avoid hurting P50 much. it also suggests use of prefix caching for repeated queries.
[04:38] Katherine: security question — is data stored in redwood? logs? where do PII traces go?
[04:45] Avery: good callout. hosted API has an option to opt-in to data retention for debugging; default is no retention. we offer SOC2 attestation, SSO via SAML, and KMS integrations for key wrapping on private deployments — hosted has envelope encryption and we provide audit logs accessible via console. i'll attach our security pack after.
[05:08] Liam: do you do on-prem private control plane if we need it down the line?
[05:11] Avery: yes, Redwood Private is an option — same API surface but customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem nodes for extreme regulatory needs.
[05:20] Diego: back to reranker internals — we accept either text-only candidates or precomputed embeddings. when embeddings are sent we skip the local embed inference, saving latency. reranker scoring is optimized: we do cross-attention on candidate pairs but a lot of infra-level tricks — quant-friendly kernels, continuous batching, and we can serve 1-2 ms per doc on the light family at lower sequence lengths. those numbers vary with sequence length/candidate count.
[06:05] Priya: if we send top-50 candidates from our vec db, what's a realistic rerank latency?
[06:10] Diego: for light model family, median for 50 candidates at 256 tokens per doc is around 80-120 ms, 95th around 250-320 ms. for heavy family maybe 180-300ms median. again depends on model and doc size.
[06:35] Jonah: we need P50 <200ms — might be ok with light family. cost tradeoffs?
[06:42] Avery: light family often halves the per-call cost versus heavy. Optimize will give you expected $/qps given your distribution. Diego can sketch a quick cost table.
[06:55] Diego: (shares slide) two modes: synchronous rerank and async streaming. streaming is mostly for gen endpoints; rerank is synchronous. Our pricing breaks down to per-embedding upsert + per-rerank call compute units; e.g. for your 200 qps with avg 30 candidates we'd estimate X compute units, i'll finalize after we see your logs.
[07:20] Jonah: an aside — we use Infralytix on some internal proofs, they have a cheaper per-call rate but we've seen quality issues.
[07:28] Diego: noted. some customers do hybrid — cheap vector retrieval vendor + redwood rerank for final scoring.
[07:34] Priya: latency jitter — do you have metrics and tracing hooks? we need to trace per-request token costs.
[07:40] Diego: yes console exposes traces per route, token-level cost breakdown, and we have trace hooks to inject IDs into headers for correlation with your logs.
[07:50] Katherine: do you support SSO roles and RBAC for the console? we need admin/control plane separation.
[07:56] Avery: yes SAML + SCIM provisioning, role-based teams, and audit logs with retention policies.
[08:05] Jonah: can you run a small bench with our corpus? we'd like raw numbers.
[08:10] Avery: that's the typical next step — priya would drop a sanitized portion of logs and a corpus, diego will spin up a bench and return results in a shared sheet.
[08:18] Priya: we can do that, probably a month of queries ~ 2m rows. we'll redact PII.
[08:22] Diego: perfect — for benching we prefer a sample of 10-20k queries representing tail and head. also include query lat and candidate sizes.
[08:32] Jonah: do you have examples of rerank configs that improved MRR?
[08:36] Diego: yes — in our repo we keep examples: boosting recency features, candidate dedup weights, and a small negative sampling config to de-emphasize near-duplicate docs. i'll attach the example rerank yaml.
[08:49] [00:09:00] Sana (Product): small note — Optimize also surfaces quantization recommendations. for workloads like MarineGate with long docs we sometimes suggest int8 for rerank to reduce mem and cost but run evals to check for quality regressions.
[09:10] Priya: int8 — do you do that server-side or do we quantize our model?
[09:14] Diego: server-side, we host quantized variants and the runtime selects kernel paths. there may be minor quality delta on some corpora; Optimize flags likely regressions by prompt set.
[09:28] Liam: what about multi-region failover? our traffic splits east/west.
[09:33] Avery: hosted API supports region routing; you can set region preference per route and have fallback to another region or a cheaper model family. we also support multi-region dedicated pools for Reserved capacity.
[09:47] Jonah: procurement question — is there a minimum committed spend for reserved?
[09:51] Avery: Dedicated has monthly min commits, but hosted has no long-term commitment. if you want predictable latency and concurrency we can propose a Dedicated pool estimate.
[10:02] Katherine: auditability — do we get raw request logs for compliance?
[10:07] Avery: you can opt into extended logging. default is basic metrics; extended logging with payload retention is opt-in and we recommend using KMS for key material in Private.
[10:18] Priya: hmm cost of storing logs?
[10:20] Avery: billed as an add-on — we'll send the pricing sheet.
[10:25] Jonah: any examples of customers with similar size corpora?
[10:28] Diego: yes — "HarborBay" and "Stonegate" are in our case studies, both had 10-20m docs and used rerank with light family to meet latency. i'll send anonymized bench results.
[10:40] Liam: ok let's look at an end-to-end demo hit.
[10:44] Diego: i'll call the hosted flow — first step we hit embeddings endpoint for one doc to show vector creation (curl live).
[10:52] [screen share showing terminal — some typos in command]
[11:05] Diego: curl -X POST api.redwood-infer/v1/embeds upsert -d '{"docs": [{"id":"123","text":"ship hull corrosion guidance"}] }' — response returns vector id and dims. note: the sample snippet in the deck has a stray bracket, sorry about that.
[11:22] Priya: our vec db uses 1536-dim, fine. next?
[11:26] Diego: then we simulate retrieval by grabbing top 50 doc ids and call rerank: POST /v1/rerank with query + candidates (embedding field included). (shows response) it returns scores sorted, and you can request explanation tokens we surface as highlights. sometimes speech-to-text in transcripts shows that as "explanash" so ignore that.
[11:52] Jonah: explainability — how do highlights work?
[11:56] Diego: it's a logits-based saliency, we map high attention tokens back to spans and return offsets. not perfect but useful. we can also return attribution scores per candidate.
[12:10] Priya: any rate limits? we will need burst handling.
[12:14] Avery: hosted has tiered rate limits. we provide burst allowances; if you need guaranteed throughput we advise Dedicated. we can set per-route quotas in console.
[12:28] Liam: how about canary rollouts? we want to test new models without impacting 100% of traffic.
[12:33] Diego: console supports canary % and automatic rollback on error thresholds. you can also configure A/B experiments with different rerank configs.
[12:44] Jonah: are there connectors for our vector db? we use VectorBox.
[12:48] Diego: we have out-of-the-box connectors for many vendors; for others we provide a sample integration script (Python snippet) to orchestrate retrieval+call reranker.
[12:58] Priya: ok for benching, what env do you need?
[13:02] Diego: a sanitized bundle: sample queries (10-20k), candidate sets for each, and optional relevance labels for eval. with that we will run rerank and produce MRR/latency/cost tables.
[13:15] [13:15] Priya: we can export a month of queries with user IDs removed — i'll aim for 10k representative.
[13:20] Avery: perfect. we'll also provide a shared sheet for results.
[13:24] Jonah: how do we instrument our code for token-costs?
[13:27] Diego: inject the request-id header and correlate with console traces; we expose token counters and per-request cost in the response metadata when enabled.
[13:37] Liam: question — in a scenario where the vector retrieval vendor is cheaper but lower recall, can we do hybrid where rerank uses external retrieval and we run a lightweight recall pass inside redwood?
[13:48] Diego: yes hybrid retrieval is common: external vendor for top-500, then internally run a fast candidate expansion or lexical pass to add missing docs, then rerank. optimization page suggests config for expansion size.
[14:05] Sana: small product note — Optimize will generate a recommended quantization profile and batch settings; it surfaces estimated quality lift and compute savings, and allows you to accept the changes which will create a rollout in the console.
[14:20] Priya: can we run Optimize recommendations in a dry-run mode? we want to see suggested batch sizes and the impact.
[14:26] Diego: yes dry-run — it runs on a copy of traffic and reports expected latency/cost but doesn't change production.
[14:34] Jonah: let's talk SLAs — we need 99.9 availability and a P99 latency SLO.
[14:41] Avery: for hosted we offer best-effort; Dedicated has SLA options. for mission-critical we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[14:51] Katherine: outage recovery — do you have runbook integrations like PagerDuty?
[14:55] Avery: yes PagerDuty, Datadog, and webhooks. we also provide per-route error metrics in the console.
[15:03] [15:03] Diego: shifting to sample rerank config — here's a minimal yaml: rerank: model: rwd-rank-light-v2 top_k: 50 features: [recency, click_rate, doc_length] negative_sampling: hard_examples_weight: 0.25 you can pass custom features from your metadata.
[15:28] Priya: we have featurized meta like vessel_type, publication_date — can those be consumed?
[15:32] Diego: yes pass them in candidate metadata and map names in rerank schema. they can be scalar or categorical.
[15:40] Jonah: will this require retraining? or is reranker using zero-shot scoring?
[15:44] Diego: hosted reranker supports zero-shot scoring; you can also provide labeled examples and run a fine-tuning flow if you want better signal. we also support lightweight click-based online shaping.
[15:58] Liam: fine-tuning on our data — is that in hosted?
[16:01] Avery: yes hosted supports supervised fine-tuning with private datasets; we store fine-tune artifacts in customer-controlled buckets and provide audit logs.
[16:10] Priya: what's the turnaround time for a bench?
[16:13] Diego: typically 3-5 business days once we have representative data; faster if you give a smaller sample.
[16:21] Jonah: ok let's outline next steps now.
[16:24] Avery: recap: 1) MarineGate to share 10-20k queries + candidate sets (Priya) 2) Redwood to run bench and provide MRR/latency/cost sheet (Diego) 3) Redwood to send quickstart + rerank examples + security pack (Avery) 4) schedule 30m bench review (everyone)
[16:46] Priya: noted — i'll get that by end of week.
[16:49] Liam: timeline — procurement looking to finalize vendor in 4 weeks, so we need concrete bench numbers this week / next.
[16:57] Avery: we'll prioritize.
[17:00] Jonah: any blockers around contracts or infosec? we have a checklist.
[17:04] Avery: we'll send the SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, and a sample DPA. if you need a higher classification we can talk Private.
[17:11] Katherine: do you support IP allowlisting for control plane?
[17:15] Diego: yes IP allowlist and mutual TLS for some integrations.
[17:20] [closing]
[17:20] Avery: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the bench.
[17:24] Liam: thanks, appreciate the demo.
[17:26] Priya: thanks all.
